plans.price: Free (self-serve signup at tracxn.com/signup). Described as non-commercial use and 'may become unavailable in the future'. CONFIRMED.
plans.what_you_get: Premium-style access to the full curated database (7.7M+ companies, 290K+ investors, 1.8M+ funding rounds, 226K+ acquisitions) but metered. CONFIRMED limits: 200 export credits per month, 1 report download per day, NO API, no taxonomy features, no Live Deals, no collaboration/sharing; limits reset on the 1st of each month, access is 'significantly restricted' once hit. 317K Lite signups to date (Q1FY27 deck). Adequate for a coverage smoke-test, not for production.

plans.price: No public price - 'Contact Sales'. INFERRED benchmarks from Tracxn's own disclosure: FY26 revenue INR 84.0 Cr across 2,289 accounts = median account ~INR 3.7 lakh/yr (~USD 4.3K); the annual report's account tiers show only 45 accounts >INR 30L (~USD 36K) and 23 accounts >INR 40L (~USD 48K), i.e. even large enterprise seat deals are typically well under USD 60K/yr. Billing: recurring annual licence fee for seat-based access, typically billed upfront; ~75% of FY26 billings were annual subscriptions; non-refundable and auto-renewing with 30 days' notice to cancel (terms of use).
plans.what_you_get: Everything in Lite plus unrestricted access, team plan, custom taxonomy, custom reports and analysis, Deal Flow CRM, Live Deals, 24/7 support (live chat, email, WhatsApp). Economics scale with number of seats, explicitly NOT with the customer's AUM or deal volume (annual report) - favourable for a fee-earning advisory firm. Third-party (Vendr) lists six Tracxn SKUs: Small Team, Large Team, Group Pack, Corporate, Enterprise Wide Access Plan, Unlimited API Access Plan - THIRD-PARTY, unpriced.

plans.price: Volume-based pricing, no public rate card. Two licence families CONFIRMED on the pricing page: 'Internal Usage License Packs' and 'Commercial Redistribution License Packs', with customisable tiers, trial packs, tapered volume discounts and non-profit discounts. Enquiry is via a Google Form / apidesk@tracxn.com. INFERRED: priced per unique records/companies pulled, in packs.
plans.what_you_get: CONFIRMED delivery options: (1) Tracxn APIs for real-time access and custom ad-hoc queries; (2) scheduled SFTP data dumps in custom formats; (3) Snowflake share; (4) Google BigQuery sync. Datasets: companies, legal entities, investors, funding rounds, acquisitions, financials, cap tables, employee-count trends, people, news, sectors/taxonomy. Endpoint list, auth scheme, pagination size and rate limits are NOT published - UNCONFIRMED, must be obtained under NDA.

plans.price: Included for paid subscriptions with 'MCP access' - which plans qualify and any call limits are UNCONFIRMED.
plans.what_you_get: CONFIRMED: MCP server ('Tracxn Connector for Claude') giving Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and the Claude Excel add-in real-time access to companies, funding rounds, investors, M&A/IPO events, 3,000+ sector feeds, and registry financials/cap tables for 30+ countries; authenticate with a Tracxn account. Plus an on-platform AI assistant and beta agentic workflows (deal diligence, competitor benchmarking, sector landscaping). Directly relevant if JCAI wants Tracxn data inside its own Claude/Salesforce workflow rather than a bulk feed.

api_access: Yes for paying customers only (Lite explicitly excludes API). Marketing page confirms REST APIs plus scheduled SFTP dumps, Snowflake and BigQuery delivery; CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Affinity, Pipedrive), Google Sheets and Excel plugins, Chrome/Firefox extensions, iOS/Android apps, and an MCP connector. Technical specifics - authentication method, endpoint paths, page size (the often-cited '20 records per call' could NOT be verified), rate limits, sandbox availability - are all UNCONFIRMED because the API documentation sits behind login; request it from apidesk@tracxn.com before signing. Terms of use prohibit crawlers/scrapers and any bulk extraction 'unless explicitly permitted by Us through APIs', so bulk ingestion REQUIRES the data-solutions licence, not the seat plan.
archive_window: No stated start date - UNCONFIRMED. INFERRED from evidence: the company was founded in 2012 and the acquisitions database was only launched in the 2017-19 period, so pre-2013 M&A is back-filled rather than natively collected and should be treated as thin. Public geography pages chart activity year by year and quote 'last 5 years' aggregates; the Japan page reports 5,055 lifetime IPOs and 1,263 lifetime acquisitions, implying multi-decade history for listed events but shallow depth for private deals. Financials carry 1/3/5-year CAGR and examples spanning ~FY2019-20 to FY2023-24, i.e. roughly 5 years of statements per company. Data-quality warning: Japan's page shows 126 acquisitions in Jan-Sep 2026 vs only 77 for full-year 2025, which points to recent-period over-weighting or restatement rather than a genuine surge.
data_types: Per COMPANY: description and business model, proprietary sector/business-model taxonomy (3,000+ feeds, 55K+ nodes), founding year, location, employee count plus monthly growth trend (headcount data expanded to 3.4M entities globally, 850K companies in India), revenue and detailed financials (revenue data 2.8-3.1M companies; detailed financials 6.7-7.2M companies across 20+ countries incl. Japan, South Korea, India, UK, Germany, France, Italy, Singapore, Australia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines), cap table / shareholding and valuation history (419K-1.7M companies, 15+ countries - Japan IS named in the annual report's cap-table country list; the Q1FY27 deck's cap-table list names South Korea and Indonesia but not Japan), funding rounds with amount, stage, date, lead and participating investors, pre/post-money valuation and revenue multiple, acquisitions and strategic investments made, exit/IPO details, competitors and benchmarking (traffic, app rank, Tracxn Score, editor ratings), founders/executives/board with bios and social links plus an employee directory, LinkedIn/email contact, curated news (funding, M&A, leadership changes, launches), unicorn/soonicorn/minicorn status, legal-entity layer (~66M entities: registry financials, directors, cross-directorships, loans and charges, patents, trademarks, legal cases, corporate tree structures ~60K entities). Per ACQUISITION: acquirer, target, deal date, deal type, disclosed value, links to both parties' profiles, funding history, investors and valuation where disclosed; filterable by acquirer type, target sector, geography, deal size, timeline. 'Valuation exact across M&A deals and funding rounds' is flagged as UPCOMING in Q1FY27 - i.e. deal values are today largely limited to what was publicly disclosed. Also: investor profiles (290K+, 50+ filters, portfolios, co-investor networks, exits, fund lifecycles), Live Deals (curated live mandates), 11.4K+ analyst reports, and a Tracxn Private Market Index (TPX) sentiment series for 18 countries + global.
formats: Web platform (100+ filters, export of full datasets or one-pagers), Excel/Google Sheets plugins, CSV/Excel exports (Lite capped at 200 export credits/month), REST API (JSON assumed - UNCONFIRMED), scheduled SFTP dumps in custom formats, Snowflake share, BigQuery sync, Chrome/Firefox extensions, iOS/Android apps, MCP connector, email newsletters and alerts. Language: platform and outputs are English only (CONFIRMED by observation); Tracxn ingests non-English sources and the annual report names German, French, Swedish, Korean, Dutch, Greek, Finnish and Italian - Japanese is NOT in that list, a material signal for Japan-source coverage.
update_frequency: Continuous / near real-time. CONFIRMED: 7.4K+ companies added per day; 981M web domains scanned; 'AI algorithm continuously scans hundreds of signals across millions of data points to detect changes' with 'near real-time monitoring'; skilled analysts validate critical updates; customers can trigger 'Refresh & curate' workflows on demand with 24/7 support; TPX index refreshes daily. No contractual SLA is published - UNCONFIRMED.
limitations: 1) ASIA IS THIN OUTSIDE INDIA. Asia is only ~6.4% of tracked acquisitions (~3.9% ex-India) versus ~48% North America and ~31% Europe. Japan has just 55,741 companies and 1,263 lifetime acquisitions on record - against ~1.9M US companies. Korea, Taiwan, HK and SEA ex-Singapore have no published counts at all. 2) STARTUP / VC-DEAL SKEW. The taxonomy, unicorn framing and funded-company emphasis are venture-centric; the annual report claims 'enterprise grade data across high-tech as well as traditional industries', but 7M+ of the 7.7M companies are unfunded shells of coverage and depth on traditional owner-managed SMEs is unproven. 3) M&A IS A SECONDARY DATASET. The acquisitions DB was launched only in 2017-19, exact deal valuations are still an 'upcoming' feature, and disclosed value is the only value field - so deal-value disclosure rates for Asian mid-market deals will be low. 4) PUBLISHED NUMBERS ARE INCONSISTENT, which is itself a due-diligence flag: companies 7.7M (homepage/AR) vs '8M+' (API page) vs 3.3M (Lite page); acquisitions 226K+ (homepage) vs '200K+' (product page); funding rounds 1.8M vs 1.3M; cap tables 133K vs 419K vs 1.7M; investors 290K vs 250K; the North America page contradicts itself on acquisitions (109,414 vs 119,651) and unicorns (891 vs 1,285). 5) NO JAPANESE-LANGUAGE INGESTION IS CLAIMED and there is no Japanese UI; EDINET/TDnet-grade Japanese filing depth should not be assumed. 6) LICENCE FRICTION. Terms of use forbid redistribution, republication or automated extraction and restrict use to internal business purposes with attribution; anything client-facing or bulk needs a Commercial Redistribution licence. Governing law is India, exclusive jurisdiction Bangalore courts - unusual for a Japanese firm's vendor contract. 7) SMALL VENDOR RISK: FY26 revenue only INR 84.0 Cr (~USD 10M, -0.6% YoY), Q1FY27 EBITDA -4.2 Cr and PAT -3.0 Cr, 717 permanent employees, only 40+ sector specialists; APAC ex-India is 9% of revenue, so Japan/Korea/SEA coverage is unlikely to be a roadmap priority. 8) Public-company coverage exists mainly as an exit/IPO and benchmarking layer, not as a full listed-company fundamentals product.
ma_relevance: MEDIUM for JCAI, and asymmetric by geography. Strong fit for (a) US and Europe buyer-side longlisting - a Japanese seller looking for cross-border acquirers, where Tracxn's ~2.2M North American and ~2.8M European company records plus 109K/71K acquisition histories let you profile a strategic acquirer's whole M&A track record; (b) sector/theme mapping and competitor sets via the 3,000-feed taxonomy; (c) acquirer-profiling for corporates (who bought what, when, at what disclosed value, plus corporate tree and legal-entity layer); (d) India and Singapore work, which are Tracxn's best non-Western markets. Weak fit for (a) Japanese target sourcing - EDINET plus a domestic source is clearly better, which matches JCAI's stated plan; (b) Korea, Taiwan, HK and SEA ex-Singapore mid-market origination, where counts are unpublished and probably shallow; (c) valuation benchmarking on Asian mid-market deals, because disclosed value is sparse. The seat-based, AUM-independent pricing and the Salesforce integration plus MCP connector make it cheap to pilot inside JCAI's existing Salesforce/Claude stack. Treat Tracxn as the USA + India/SEA-tech layer of a multi-source plan, not as the single Asia M&A source.
implementation_notes: TRIAL DESIGN: (1) Start with free Tracxn Lite (200 export credits/month, 1 report/day, no API) - enough to run a blind coverage benchmark before any sales call. (2) Build a 50-deal test set from JCAI's own closed and lost mandates plus public sources, stratified as ~15 Japan mid-market, ~10 Korea/Taiwan/HK, ~10 SEA, ~10 US, ~5 Europe, deliberately including non-tech (manufacturing, logistics, healthcare services, construction) and deals under USD 20M; score each on: target found at all, acquirer found, correct date, deal value present, deal type correct, advisers named, and days-to-publish versus the announcement date. Expect a sharp drop for Japan/Korea non-tech - that gap is the 'why this plan' evidence. (3) Separately test 30 known Japanese SMEs for presence, employee count, and registry financials, and 20 US strategic acquirers for M&A-history completeness. (4) Test the MCP connector against Claude/Excel early, since it may remove the need for a data feed entirely. RFP QUESTIONS: exact company and acquisition counts for Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines (they refuse to publish these); share of acquisitions with a disclosed value by region and year; earliest reliable year for acquisitions by region; number of Japanese and Korean language analysts and what Japanese sources are ingested (TDnet? kanpo? teikoku/TSR-style registries? M&A press?); median lag from announcement to record; full API reference with auth, page size, rate limits and a sandbox key; field-level schema and a sample Japan/US extract before signing; SLA and correction turnaround; whether client-facing use in IM/teaser/pitch material is permitted and at what licence tier. NEGOTIATION LEVERS: vendor is small, loss-making and flat on revenue with APAC ex-India at 9%, so it needs logos in Japan; their own disclosure shows very few accounts above USD 36-48K/yr, so anchor there; ask for a paid pilot credited against year one, trial data-solution packs (they advertise them), tapered volume discounts, a coverage-based termination right if the 50-deal benchmark fails, seat count flexibility instead of enterprise-wide, and multi-year price protection. Push back on India-law/Bangalore-jurisdiction and on the auto-renewal with only 30 days' notice; get any client-facing (buyer/seller-facing) usage right stated explicitly, since standard terms bar redistribution.
company_background: Founded 2012 (annual report; some sources say 2013) by Neha Singh (ex-Sequoia Capital, IIT) and Abhishek Goyal (ex-Accel Partners, Amazon, Yahoo, IIT). HQ Bengaluru, India. Listed on NSE and BSE on 20 Oct 2022 as Tracxn Technologies Limited; early backers include Ratan Tata and the NRJN Family Trust. CONFIRMED financials: FY26 revenue from operations INR 84.0 Cr (-0.6% YoY; FY25 84.5, FY24 82.8, FY23 78.1, FY22 63.5, FY21 43.8); Q1FY27 revenue INR 21.1 Cr, total income 22.6 Cr, EBITDA -4.2 Cr, PAT -3.0 Cr, deferred revenue 38.8 Cr, cash 88.2 Cr. 717 permanent employees as of 31 Mar 2026; 40+ sector specialists plus module-based data teams (company profiles, funding, M&A, financials, cap tables, valuations, feeds) and a MyAnalyst support desk; closing sales team ~30-34 members scaling to 60 by Dec 2026; sales and marketing now 30% of headcount. Customers: 2,289 accounts as of 31 Mar 2026, 2,350 as of Q1FY27 (+16% YoY), across 50+ countries; top five countries by account count India, USA, UK, Singapore, Germany; mix ~50% investment industry (VC, PE, investment banks, CVC, accelerators, family offices), ~45-46% corporates (corp dev/M&A, strategy, innovation, sales, consulting, startups), rest universities/government/industry bodies; named customers include Bain Capital and Lightspeed. FY26 revenue by geography: India ~45%, Americas 25%, EMEA 21%, APAC ex-India 9%. Pure SaaS seat-subscription model, ~75% of billings annual and billed upfront; asset-light with India-based data operations as the cost advantage. Product timeline: Tracxn Score/reports/live chat 2017-19, acquisitions database and portfolio tracker 2017-19, Tracxn Lite + Legal Entities + Regulatory databases more recently, MCP connector and AI assistant in FY26/Q1FY27. Also publishes 900+ press mentions per quarter and 30M+ annualised organic visits.
confidence: HIGH for company background, financials, headcount, customer mix, revenue-by-geography, plan structure/limits for Lite, delivery channels, terms-of-use restrictions, and the per-geography company/acquisition counts for US, North America, Europe, Asia, India, China, Japan, Singapore and Israel (all taken from Tracxn's own public pages and its FY25-26 annual report and Q1FY27 investor presentation, both extracted directly from the PDFs). MEDIUM for interpretation of Asia share and the archive window. LOW / UNCONFIRMED for: seat and data-solution prices (no public rate card; benchmarks are inferred from disclosed account-tier data), API endpoint/auth/pagination/rate-limit specifics, per-country counts for South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines, deal-value disclosure rates, and Japanese-source ingestion. NOTE: WebSearch was unavailable for this session (quota exhausted at 200/200), so all findings come from direct URL fetches plus locally extracted PDFs; third-party pricing pages (G2 403, Vendr unpriced) added nothing.

name: SPEEDA (substitute candidate for the Japan/Asia layer)
operator: Uzabase, Inc. (ユーザベース), Tokyo, Japan - operator of SPEEDA, SPEEDA Expert Research and NewsPicks. Included here only as the closest Asia-native substitute/complement to Tracxn; not researched to the same depth in this pass.
docs_url: Not located in this pass - UNCONFIRMED (no public API documentation found; SPEEDA is sold as a seat-based platform with a Salesforce/Agentforce integration).
region_main: Japan-first, with Asia and global company coverage. Japanese-language platform and Japanese analyst team - the reverse of Tracxn's profile.
region_surroundings: CONFIRMED from the vendor's own Japanese site (Sep 2026): 12.7M+ companies globally, 1,800+ company attribute datasets, 3,000+ in-house industry/trend reports, 20,000+ original news articles, expert network of ~286K domestic and ~237K overseas professionals, 100+ in-house analysts, 2,500+ customer organisations, adopted by 90% of Japan's top-100 companies by market cap. NO public per-country company or M&A deal counts, and no published acquisition count - so its Asia M&A deal coverage versus Tracxn is UNCONFIRMED and would need the same 50-deal benchmark.

plans.what_you_get: Market research, industry reports, company screening and comparison, M&A sourcing, R&D and new-business evaluation; browser and mobile access; Salesforce / Agentforce integration. Positioned for Japanese corporates and advisers.

api_access: Not confirmed publicly; a Salesforce/Agentforce integration is advertised, which implies some connector-level access. UNCONFIRMED.
data_types: Company profiles and financials (Japan-heavy), 1,800+ attribute datasets, industry/trend reports written by in-house analysts, news, expert-network interviews, M&A sourcing screens. Deal-level M&A field detail UNCONFIRMED.
formats: Web platform, mobile, Salesforce/Agentforce integration; Japanese-language UI and content.
limitations: No public coverage-by-geography or deal counts, no published pricing, no confirmed API or bulk feed, and it is a Japanese-language product - so it complements EDINET on Japan and Asia qualitative depth but cannot be assessed as a US/Europe deal database. Its expert-network and report content overlaps with what JCAI advisers already do in-house.
ma_relevance: Useful as the Japan/Asia qualitative and industry-report layer alongside EDINET, and as a negotiation alternative when talking to Tracxn - but it is not a substitute for Tracxn's US/Europe transaction history, and its M&A deal database is unverified.
implementation_notes: If evaluated, run the identical 50-deal benchmark used for Tracxn, weighted to Japan and Korea/Taiwan/SEA, and ask specifically for: number of M&A transactions held, per-country company counts, whether deal records include value and advisers, export/API terms, and whether content may be reused in client-facing IM/teaser material (Japanese vendors are often restrictive here).
company_background: Uzabase, Inc., Tokyo-listed Japanese business-intelligence company; SPEEDA is its flagship B2B research platform, complemented by SPEEDA Expert Research and the NewsPicks media business. Only the SPEEDA product page was reviewed in this pass.
confidence: LOW-MEDIUM. Single-page vendor-site evidence only; no independent verification, no pricing, no deal counts. WebSearch was unavailable this session, which limited cross-checking.
